goal: Lower day-ahead 24h load-forecast MASE across all 53 EIA-930 BAs using only information a forecaster genuinely has at forecast time. Improvements must generalise, not just fit the validation split.

baseline.note: Measured on validation (calendar 2024), all 53 BAs, causal covariates.

success.note: A candidate only counts if it improves `mase` AND does not worsen `holdout_gap` by more than 0.02. A win on tuned BAs paid for by held-out BAs is overfitting, not progress.

eval_contract.split: validation (calendar 2024). Test (2025) is reserved for a single final confirmation via {"confirm": true}.
eval_contract.rejects: future_mode='oracle', and any setup whose future covariates change when post-origin actuals are perturbed

hard_constraints: Never use realized future values as future covariates. temp_c is observed ASOS data and wind_mw/solar_mw are EIA actual generation; none are knowable at forecast time. The causal guard enforces this by perturbing post-origin actuals and requiring the future covariates not to move.
Never score on the test split during search. Optimise validation only.
Do not tune the MASE denominator, the split boundaries, or the eval window to flatter a result.
Report a candidate as an improvement only when the held-out-BA score moves with the tuned score.

ideas.rationale: Measured: a flat persistence temperature is WORSE than supplying no future temperature (RTO-7 test MASE 0.7395 vs 0.5937), because a constant 24h temperature implies no diurnal cycle and the checkpoint was trained to trust real temperature. A causal proxy that preserves diurnal shape should recover much of the 0.084 MASE that oracle temperature was worth.
ideas.try: future temp_c = same-hour-yesterday (lag 24) profile; or train-set hour-of-day x day-of-year climatology; or yesterday's shape re-anchored to the last observed value; or a damped blend of climatology and persistence.

ideas.rationale: Chronos-2 uses group attention for cross-series in-context learning. A neighbouring BA's PAST load is observable at forecast time, so it is causal. Likely to help small BAs most, which is where the 53-BA macro is weakest.
ideas.try: add correlated neighbour BA load as past covariates, chosen by interconnect or by train-split correlation; keep them past-only.

ideas.rationale: surge-fm-v3 is a FULL fine-tune over only 53 series and beats zero-shot by ~4% honestly. Literature reports full fine-tuning of Chronos degrading vs LoRA on small/noisy datasets, with LoRA's low-rank constraint acting as regularisation and recommended below ~10k series.
ideas.try: LoRA r=8 alpha=16 on q,k,v,o and output_patch_embedding; lr 2e-5; early stopping on validation with patience; compare against full fine-tune at equal budget.

ideas.rationale: The current filter clips only load_mw > 200000, a global threshold. BANC has a 70 GW spike against a 1.8 GW median, inflating its MASE denominator ~60x. Five BAs affected (BANC, SPA, LGEE, SEC, TEPC). This corrupts training targets as well as the denominator.
ideas.try: per-BA robust rejection (rolling median absolute deviation, or a multiple of the BA's own median/quantile) instead of an absolute cutoff.

ideas.rationale: The nominal 80% interval covers only 71-73% (and 59% under the flat-temp path), so the probabilistic output is overconfident. Conformalized quantile regression on an independent calibration split restores coverage and often tightens intervals.
ideas.try: split-conformal / CQR adjustment fitted on validation, applied to the quantile heads. Track cov_pi80 and crps; this targets calibration, not MASE.

ideas.rationale: Cheap, low-risk capacity levers that rarely overfit.
ideas.try: context 1024/2048/4096; multi-seed or multi-checkpoint ensembling of quantiles; recency-weighted fine-tuning sampling.
